ai.title: Add Strong subscription backend with Stripe webhooks and DB migrations
ai.summary: This adds a subscription billing backend spanning packages/billing, web Stripe API routes, the internal DB layer, and the operator env schema. The new common/src/constants/subscription-plans.ts file defines SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS (100, 200, 500), DEFAULT_TIER as SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS[200], and SUBSCRIPTION_DISPLAY_NAME = 'Strong', while packages/billing/src/subscription.ts implements block-grant creation, weekly usage windows, rate limiting, and credit migration via handleSubscribe. packages/billing/src/subscription-webhooks.ts wires Stripe invoice and subscription events to handleSubscriptionInvoicePaid, handleSubscriptionInvoicePaymentFailed, handleSubscriptionUpdated, and handleSubscriptionDeleted, using createSubscriptionPriceMappings against STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_100_PRICE_ID, STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_200_PRICE_ID, and STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_500_PRICE_ID to resolve the tier.
ai.evidence: New files packages/billing/src/subscription.ts and packages/billing/src/subscription-webhooks.ts define tier logic and Stripe webhook handlers; common/src/constants/subscription-plans.ts defines SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS with tiers 100, 200, 500 and DEFAULT_TIER as SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS[200]; migrations 0036_handy_silver_sable.sql, 0037_many_millenium_guard.sql, and 0038_legal_jimmy_woo.sql (referenced by meta/0036_snapshot.json, 0037_snapshot.json, 0038_snapshot.json) create the subscription, limit_override, and subscription_status enum tables plus tier and scheduled_tier columns.
ai.migration: If you run the Freebuff service, you must set STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_100_PRICE_ID, STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_200_PRICE_ID, and STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_500_PRICE_ID and apply migrations 0036, 0037, and 0038 before Stripe webhooks can be processed.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that invokes handleSubscribe on first payment or whether the web routes are wired behind the Freebuff product surface rather than Codebuff.

changes.what: Added subscription block-grant engine, limit resolution, weekly usage tracking, rate limiting, credit migration, and Stripe webhook handlers; exported them from the billing package index.
Added tier plan constants, the SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS table keyed by price 100/200/500, DEFAULT_TIER, and a 'subscription' entry to GRANT_PRIORITIES and GrantType to support subscription-credit grants.

Added STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_*_PRICE_ID vars to the operator env schema, created the subscription_status enum, subscription and limit_override tables, tier and scheduled_tier columns, and a stripe_subscription_id column plus index on credit_ledger.
Added Stripe subscription create, change-tier, cancel, and user subscription status routes, and wired invoice/subscription webhooks to separate organization and user subscription handlers.
Added a 'subscription' grant type to the usage display breakdown so subscription credits render with a teal Zap icon alongside free, referral, purchase, admin, and ad credits.

ai.title: spawnagents clarifies agenttype vs tool names
ai.summary: Added explicit warning to `spawn-agents.ts` prompt instructing `agent_type` to accept only agent names, not tool names. Prevents misuse of `spawn_agents` for direct tool calls like `read_files` or `str_replace`. Scope limited to `common/src/tools/params/tool/spawn-agents.ts`. Reinforces existing guidance to call tools directly when not spawning agents.

eli5.text: When you ask the system to start multiple helpers at once, you must now name a real helper (like 'commander' or 'code-searcher'), not a direct action (like 'read_files' or 'str_replace'). The instructions now warn whoever uses this feature that picking a tool-name instead of a helper-name won't work, and that you should just call the tool directly if that's what you wanted. This only affects the part of the system that launches several helpers in one go, and you'd notice it right away because the wrong names are now explicitly blocked with a message.

ai.title: Add codebuff login command for remote sessions
ai.summary: Introduces `codebuff login` command to handle authentication outside the TUI, specifically for remote or SSH environments where clipboard integration fails. The new `runPlainLogin` function prints the login URL as plain text, allowing users to copy it via standard terminal selection. Updates `login-modal.tsx` to display a tip suggesting this command when `isRemoteSession()` detects an SSH connection. Implemented in `cli/src/login/plain-login.ts` with fallback logic for browser opening failures.

eli5.text: If you use Codebuff over an SSH connection to a remote server, the login process can now work without the graphical pop-up and clipboard tricks that break in remote terminals. Instead, running the login command prints a web address as plain text that you can highlight and copy with your terminal's normal copy shortcut, then paste into your browser to finish signing in. The login screen inside the tool also shows a tip telling you to do this when it detects you are connected remotely. This only matters when you are working in a terminal session that is forwarded or remote, not when running Codebuff locally on your own computer.

ai.title: Strip quotes from code search flags
ai.summary: Added quote-stripping logic to `flagsArray` in `sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts` to handle cases where flags are passed with surrounding quotes (e.g., `"'foo.md'"` → `"foo.md"`). Since `spawn()` does not perform shell interpretation, this ensures ripgrep receives clean arguments. The change applies to the SDK's code search tool. An optional `logger` parameter was also added to `codeSearch` to log ripgrep spawn details.

eli5.text: If you use the code search feature and pass in search terms wrapped in quotes, those quotes are now automatically removed before the search runs. Previously, typing something like "'filename.md'" would treat the quotes as part of the name and fail to find matches. Now the quotes are stripped, so your search works as intended. Live today.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to show you the different strategies it's considering and which one it ultimately picked, the screen will now reliably display which option was selected and why. Previously, the program looked for the selection information in the wrong place, so the chosen strategy and its reason were sometimes left blank. The fix makes it search for that information in the correct spot before displaying the result. This applies to anyone using the command-line version of the assistant and is working today.

ai.title: Thinking block collapse state now preview until next message
ai.summary: Thinking block UI replaces boolean isCollapsed with tri-state thinkingCollapseState ('expanded', 'preview', 'hidden') in types/chat.ts. Completed thinking blocks now show a 5-line preview instead of hiding content, driven by PREVIEW_LINE_COUNT in components/thinking.tsx. Scope limited to CLI components, hooks, and block utilities. Collapse-all operations map 'hidden' to thinkingCollapseState for thinking blocks while preserving isCollapsed for other block types.

eli5.text: When an AI is thinking through its response, you'll now see the last 5 lines of that thinking displayed as a preview, instead of the thinking being completely hidden after it finishes. This affects anyone using the command-line version of the AI assistant to have a conversation. If you looked at a thinking block, you'd notice it shows a few lines of the AI's internal reasoning rather than appearing completely collapsed, giving you a glimpse into what the AI was working through.
